newsitem.title: USA: U.S. court issues temporary stay of new phone rules.
newsitem.headline: U.S. court issues temporary stay of new phone rules.

text.p: A U.S. appeals court in St. Louis put a temporary freeze Friday on a sweeping set of new federal rules meant to open the $100 billion local phone market to competition, said state regulators and BellSouth Corp..

The court is considering a challenge to the Federal Communications Commission rules from Baby Bell phone companies, local companies and state regulators. The rules were to go into effect on Monday, but the court issued a stay until oral arguments are heard in the case next Thursday.

Lawyers noted that the stay issued by the court is only temporary and that what truly matters is whether the court decides to put the landmark rules on hold while the case is argued on its merits. Next week's oral arguments were expected to revolve around the issue of a longer freeze.

But lawyers also noted it was significant that the court decided to issue any kind of stay in the first place. "Often these motions to stay are dismissed without argument (by the court)," said attorney Alfred Mamlet of Steptoe & Johnson.

The FCC issued its "interconnection" orders in August in a bid to break open the local phone market to long-distance carriers, cable-television operators and other communications companies. The rules implemented the overhaul of the nation's telecommunications laws enacted earlier this year.

But local and regional phone companies as well as state regulators said the agency had overstepped its authority, and took the matter to court. The cases that were filed around the country were consolidated in the U.S. appeals court in St. Louis.
